# Introduction

In South Africa, many households lack reliable access to electricity, clean drinking water and adequate sanitation. Government departments need evidence showing which service gaps are most closely linked to poverty limited infrastructure budgets can be allocated effectively.

## Decision problem
Which basic services(electricity, water and sanitation) are most strongly associated with household poverty, and which should be prioritised for intervention?

###stakeholders
- Government
- Municipalities
- NGOs

### needs and objectives
Stakeholders need evidence evaluating which service gaps has the strongest relationship withi household income and wellbeing.

objectives:
- Identify the relationship between basic services and poverty.
- Produce evidence that supports Infrastructure investment decisions.

## Success Critria
- Identify meaningful relationships
- Use Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
- Present results to a range of audiences

###task
- explore the household survey data
- Compare income, electricity and water and sanitation attributes
- Produce Data findings in the form of data visualisations

### Risks and Assumptions
- Missing values
- Duplicated records
- Placeholder codes

## 1.5 Dataset Portfolio Overview

```{r overview}
portfolio <- tibble(
  Dataset             = c("df05_BS", "df06_HE", "Df07_HW", "df09_HR"),
  Name                = c("Basic Services", "Household Energy",
                           "Household Wellbeing", "Household Resources"),
  Unit_of_observation = rep("Household", 4),
  Rows                = c(nrow(df05_BS), nrow(df06_HE), nrow(Df07_HW), nrow(df09_HR)),
```

## 1.6 Keys and Relationships

`HouseholdID` is the identifier by all four datasets.
Beware of data overlap though relationship types between the different data sources.

```{r key-summary}
key_summary <- tibble(
  Dataset                    = c("df05_BS", "df06_HE", "Df07_HW", "df09_HR"),
  Rows                       = c(nrow(df05_BS), nrow(df06_HE), nrow(Df07_HW), nrow(df09_HR)),
  Unique_HouseholdID         = c(n_distinct(df05_BS$HouseholdID), n_distinct(df06_HE$HouseholdID),
                                  n_distinct(Df07_HW$HouseholdID), n_distinct(df09_HR$HouseholdID)),
  Duplicate_HouseholdID_rows = Rows - Unique_HouseholdID
)
```


#2. Data Quality Assessment

## 2.1 Completeness

```{r missing}
# missing values
sum(is.na(df05_BS))
colSums(is.na(df05_BS))

sum(is.na(df06_HE))
colSums(is.na(df06_HE))

sum(is.na(Df07_HW))
colSums(is.na(Df07_HW))

sum(is.na(df09_HR))
colSums(is.na(df09_HR))
```
```{r missing-plot}
# combine the non-zero missing counts into one plot
missing_summary <- function(df, name) {
  df %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Missing") %>%
    filter(Missing > 0) %>%
    mutate(Dataset = name) %>%
    relocate(Dataset)
}

missingness <- bind_rows(
  missing_summary(df05_BS, "df05_BS"), missing_summary(df06_HE, "df06_HE"),
  missing_summary(Df07_HW, "Df07_HW"), missing_summary(df09_HR, "df09_HR")
)

kable(missingness, caption = "Variables with explicit missing (NA) values")

ggplot(missingness, aes(x = reorder(paste(Dataset, Variable), Missing), y = Missing, fill = Dataset)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Explicit missing values (NA) by variable", x = NULL, y = "Missing records") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 2.5 Data Types
```{r data-types}
type_table <- function(df, name) {
  tibble(Dataset = name, Variable = names(df), Type = map_chr(df, ~ class(.)[1]))
}

bind_rows(
  type_table(df05_BS, "df05_BS"), type_table(df06_HE, "df06_HE"),
  type_table(Df07_HW, "Df07_HW"), type_table(df09_HR, "df09_HR")
) %>%
  count(Dataset, Type) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Type, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  kable(caption = "Count of variables by R data type, per dataset")
```

## 2.6 Distributions and Unusual Observations

```{r distributions-income-stats}
Df07_HW %>%
  mutate(Income_clean = ifelse(TotalMonthlyHouseholdIncomeRaw >= 9999999, NA, TotalMonthlyHouseholdIncomeRaw)) %>%
  summarise(
    Min    = min(Income_clean, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(Income_clean, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean   = round(mean(Income_clean, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
    Max    = max(Income_clean, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD     = round(sd(Income_clean, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
    N_flagged_as_placeholder = sum(is.na(Income_clean) & !is.na(TotalMonthlyHouseholdIncomeRaw))
  ) %>%
  kable(caption = "Household monthly income (Rand) after placeholder removal")

income_clean <- Df07_HW %>% mutate(Income_clean = ifelse(TotalMonthlyHouseholdIncomeRaw >= 9999999, NA, TotalMonthlyHouseholdIncomeRaw))
boxplot(income_clean$Income_clean,horizontal = TRUE )
```

```{r distributions-income-plot}
Df07_HW %>%
  mutate(Income_clean = ifelse(TotalMonthlyHouseholdIncomeRaw >= 9999999, NA, TotalMonthlyHouseholdIncomeRaw)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Income_clean)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Income_clean)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#2c7fb8") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma, trans = "log1p",
                      breaks = c(0, 1000, 5000, 20000, 100000)) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of household monthly income (log scale)",
```

#3. Exploratory Data Analysis

The EDA of whether access to basic services appears related to household poverty.

### df05_BS - Basic Services

```{r water}
barplot(table(df05_BS$WaterSafeCode), main="Water Safety",ylab = "amount",xlab = "water Safty code")
df05_BS %>%
  count(WaterSafeCode) %>%
  mutate(Pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  kable(caption = "WaterSafeCode frequency (assumed 1 = considered safe, 2 = not safe, 9 = don't know)")
```
```{r eda-df05_BS-water-province}
df05_BS %>%
  filter(WaterSafeCode %in% c(1, 2)) %>%
  mutate(WaterSafeCode = factor(WaterSafeCode, labels = c("Considered safe", "Not considered safe"))) %>%
  count(Province, WaterSafeCode) %>%
  group_by(Province) %>%
  mutate(Pct = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Province, Pct * (WaterSafeCode == "Not considered safe")), y = Pct, fill = WaterSafeCode)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(title = "Perceived drinking water safety by province", x = NULL, y = "Share of households", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r sanitation}
barplot(table(df05_BS$MainToiletCode), main="Main Toilet Type", xlab = "toilet code", ylab = "Households")
df05_BS %>%
  filter(MainToiletCode != 99) %>%
  count(MainToiletCode) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(factor(MainToiletCode), n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#756bb1") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "MainToiletCode frequency excluding outliers", x = "Toilet code", y = "Households") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### df06_HE - Household Energy

```{r electricity}
barplot(table(df06_HE$ElectricityAccessCode), main="Electricity Access", xlab = "electricity access code", ylab = "fequency")
df06_HE %>%
  count(ElectricityAccessCode) %>%
  mutate(Pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  kable(caption = "ElectricityAccessCode frequency (assumed 1 = has access, 2 = no access, 9 = don't know)")
```

```{r loadshed}
barplot(table(df06_HE$LoadsheddingFrequencyCode), main="Loadshedding Frequency", xlab =" Loadshedding Frequency Codes", ylab = "Households")
df06_HE %>%
  filter(LoadsheddingFrequencyCode != 88) %>%
  count(LoadsheddingFrequencyCode) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(LoadsheddingFrequencyCode), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#e6550d") +
  labs(title = "Load-shedding frequency among relevant grid-connected households",
       x = "LoadsheddingFrequencyCode", y = "Households") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r eda-df06_HE-electricity-province}
df06_HE %>%
  filter(ElectricityAccessCode %in% c(1, 2)) %>%
  mutate(ElectricityAccessCode = factor(ElectricityAccessCode, labels = c("Has access", "No access"))) %>%
  count(Province, ElectricityAccessCode) %>%
  group_by(Province) %>%
  mutate(Pct = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(ElectricityAccessCode == "No access") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Province, Pct), y = Pct)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#de2d26") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(title = "Share of households without electricity access, by province", x = NULL, y = "Share without access") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### df09_HR - Household Resources

```{r assets}
table(Df07_HW$AdultHungerCode)
barplot(table(df09_HR$FridgeAssetCode), main="Fridge Ownership")
barplot(table(df09_HR$TVAssetCode), main="TV Ownership")
barplot(table(df09_HR$VehicleAssetCode), main="Vehicle Ownership")
asset_cols <- c(Fridge = "FridgeAssetCode", TV = "TVAssetCode", Computer = "ComputerAssetCode",
                 WashingMachine = "WashingMachineAssetCode", Vehicle = "VehicleAssetCode",
                 Geyser = "GeyserAssetCode", SolarPanel = "SolarPanelAssetCode")

asset_ownership <- map_dfr(names(asset_cols), function(nm) {
  col <- asset_cols[[nm]]
  df09_HR %>%
    filter(.data[[col]] %in% c(1, 2)) %>%
    summarise(Asset = nm, Pct_owning = mean(.data[[col]] == 1))
})

asset_ownership %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Asset, Pct_owning), y = Pct_owning)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#08519c") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(title = "Household asset ownership rates (assumed 1 = owns, 2 = does not own)", x = NULL, y = "Share of households") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r income-source}
barplot(table(df09_HR$MainIncomeSourceCode), main="Main Income Source", ylab = "Household freq", xlab = "income code")

asset_cols <- c("FridgeAssetCode", "TVAssetCode", "ComputerAssetCode",
                 "WashingMachineAssetCode", "VehicleAssetCode",
                 "GeyserAssetCode", "SolarPanelAssetCode")

pct_owning <- sapply(df09_HR[asset_cols], function(x) mean(x == 1, na.rm = TRUE))
names(pct_owning) <- c("Fridge", "TV", "Computer",
                 "WashingMachine", "Vehicle",
                 "Geyser", "SolarPanel")
barplot(pct_owning, horiz = TRUE, las = 1,
        main = "Household asset ownership rate", xlab = "Share of households")

df09_HR %>%
  count(MainIncomeSourceCode) %>%
  filter(!is.na(MainIncomeSourceCode)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  kable(caption = "MainIncomeSourceCode frequency")
```

## Initial Hypotheses

1. Households without electricity access are more likely to have lower incomes.
2. Unsafe water access is associated with poorer household wellbeing.
3. Households with fewer assets tend to report lower income.
4. Food insecurity appears more common among lower-income households.
